reason: This passage (Genesis 2-3) depicts the Fall of Man and demonstrates the opposite of the stated principle. When God questions Adam about eating the forbidden fruit, Adam responds with deflection and blame ('The woman you gave me...'), not humility. Similarly, the woman blames the serpent rather than accepting responsibility. The passage illustrates the consequences of failing to accept divine authority and criticism with humility, ending in divine judgment and expulsion from Eden. There is no presentation of humility in the face of criticism as a model for good leadership; instead, the narrative shows the negative results of evasion and blame-shifting.
